part.outpost.title: Outposts
part.outpost.summary: A square no enemy pawn can reach is weak; a piece there, supported by a pawn, occupies an outpost, as long as the opponent cannot trade it.
ex.po.Rj4pW: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.po.Rj4pW.hint: Your knight on f5 sits on an outpost, near the black king. See which squares it reaches.
ex.po.Rj4pW.solution: 17.Ng7#! The knight leaves the f5 outpost with check, and the queen on b4 covers e7 and f8. If 17.Nd6+, the king goes to f8 and escapes; if 17.Qxd4, the d7-pawn advances and opens the c8-bishop against the knight.
ex.po.YuOaj: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.po.YuOaj.hint: Look for a weak square near the black king for your knight on e5, with the support of a pawn.
ex.po.YuOaj.solution: 36.Ng6#! The knight goes to g6, supported by the f5-pawn, with check: it covers e5, the rook on g2 covers the g-file, and the king on f2 covers e3 and f3. If 36.Rg4+, the king captures the knight on e5 and escapes.
ex.po.fc5JB: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.po.fc5JB.hint: Your knight on d5 sits on an outpost. See which square near the black king it defends.
ex.po.fc5JB.solution: 15.Qxe7#! The queen captures the bishop on e7 with mate, defended by the outpost knight on d5.
ex.po.AYvMf: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.po.AYvMf.hint: Your knight on e5 sits on an outpost, next to the black king. Count the squares the king has.
ex.po.AYvMf.solution: 36.Nf7#! The knight leaves the e5 outpost with check: the rook on b7 covers c7, d7 and e7, and the pawn on d4 covers c5 and e5.
ex.po.YUpNF: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.po.YUpNF.hint: Your knight on e5 sits on an outpost. Look for a square from which it attacks several black pieces.
ex.po.YUpNF.solution: 18.Nxg6+! The knight leaves the outpost with check and attacks the queen and the rook on h8. After 18...hxg6 the h-file opens, and 19.Qxh8+ captures the rook.
ex.po.cdyRL: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.po.cdyRL.hint: Your knight on e5 sits on an outpost. Look for a check with it that also attacks another piece.
ex.po.cdyRL.solution: 25.Ng6+! The knight leaves the outpost with check and attacks the queen on e7. After 25...Kg8, 26.Nxe7+ captures the queen. If 25.Nxf7+, the queen recaptures, and Black is better.
ex.po.4Y6H6: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.po.4Y6H6.hint: Look for a weak square near the black king for your knight on g4, from which it attacks two pieces.
ex.po.4Y6H6.solution: 30.Nf6+! The knight enters f6, supported by the e5-pawn, with check, and attacks the bishop on e4: it is a fork. After 30...Kg7, 31.Nxe4 captures the bishop. If 30.Nxh6+, the bishop on f8 captures the knight: on h6 it has no pawn support.
ex.po.7kK73: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.po.7kK73.hint: In the centre there is a square no black pawn can reach, supported by one of your pawns. Take the c5-knight there and see what it attacks.
ex.po.7kK73.solution: 16.Ne4! The knight goes to e4, supported by the d3-pawn: the black d4-pawn has gone past that square, and Black has no f-pawn. It attacks the queen and the bishop on f6; after 16...Qc7, 17.Nxf6+. If 16.fxg5, the queen captures the knight on c5; if 16.b4, the knight on f5 goes to h4 and attacks the queen.
ex.po.uISFb: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.po.uISFb.hint: Your knight on f5 sits on an outpost. Look for a check with it that also attacks another piece.
ex.po.uISFb.solution: 24.Nh6+! The knight leaves the outpost with check and attacks the rook on f7. After 24...Kg7, 25.Nxf7 wins the rook, defended by the rook on d7.
part.openFile.title: Files and the seventh rank
part.openFile.summary: The rook is usually worth more on a useful line: the open file, the half-open file against the opponent's pawn, and the seventh rank. If the file leads nowhere, occupying it does not pay off.
ex.of.BnCSx: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.of.BnCSx.hint: Look at the squares around the black king: which ones does your queen already cover?
ex.of.BnCSx.solution: 34.Re8#! The rook goes down the open e-file with check, defended by the queen on d7, which also covers e7, f7 and g7.
ex.of.effQ7: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.of.effQ7.hint: The f-file is open all the way to the eighth rank. Notice the queen on g7 and the bishop on e5.
ex.of.effQ7.solution: 23.Rf8#! The rook goes up the open f-file with check. The queen on g7 is pinned by the bishop on e5: it can neither capture the rook nor go to g8.
ex.of.2qf9p: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.of.2qf9p.hint: Look for the line that leads to the black king.
ex.of.2qf9p.solution: 19.Rxh7#! The rook captures the h7-pawn along the half-open file, defended by the knight on f6, which also covers g8. The queen on g5 covers h6.
ex.of.CDGf1: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.of.CDGf1.hint: Count the free squares around the black king and see who covers them.
ex.of.CDGf1.solution: 39.Rf7#! The rook enters the seventh rank with check, defended by the bishop on b3. The rook on d8 covers the eighth rank, and the white king covers h6.
ex.of.qfLIc: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.of.qfLIc.hint: Look for an open file that takes your rook to an undefended black piece.
ex.of.qfLIc.solution: 19.Rd1! The rook takes the open d-file and pins the undefended bishop on d4 to the king on d7. After 19...Ke8, 20.Rxd4 captures the bishop.
ex.of.1aZOH: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.of.1aZOH.hint: The c-file is half-open for you: the only pawn on it is the black one on c4. Look at what stands behind it.
ex.of.1aZOH.solution: 29.Rxc4! The rook captures the c4-pawn along the half-open file and pins the queen on c7 to the king on c8. After 29...Bh2+ 30.Kf2, the queen is still pinned and is lost.
ex.of.bCGCV: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.of.bCGCV.hint: Your rook on g7 is on the seventh rank. Look for a check with it that also attacks another piece.
ex.of.bCGCV.solution: 40.Rd7+! The rook runs along the seventh rank to d7 with check, defended by the e6-pawn, and attacks the bishop on d6. After 40...Ke8, 41.Rxd6 captures the bishop.
ex.of.zqb96: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.of.zqb96.hint: The f-file is open, and your knight on e6 occupies an outpost near the black king. See which squares it covers.
ex.of.zqb96.solution: 19.Rxf8+! The rook captures the bishop on f8 along the open file. The king cannot recapture, because the outpost knight on e6 covers f8. After 19...Ke7, 20.Bg5#.
ex.of.QaCea: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.of.QaCea.hint: Your rooks are doubled on the open f-file, and your knight on d6 occupies an outpost near the black king.
ex.of.QaCea.solution: 26.Rf7+! The rook enters the seventh rank with check, defended by the other rook. After 26...Rxf7, 27.Rxf7#: the outpost knight on d6 defends f7 and covers e8, and the e5-pawn covers f6.
part.worstPiece.title: Improving the worst piece
part.worstPiece.summary: When there is no tactic or threat, find the piece doing the least and take it to a better square: often it is the one that creates the tactic. First, check the checks and captures.
ex.wp.own1: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.wp.own1.hint: Which white piece has not left home yet? Take it to a square from which it attacks something.
ex.wp.own1.solution: 1.Nc3! The b1 knight comes out and attacks the d5 bishop a second time. The bishop cannot move, because the d1 rook would capture the d8 rook, and only the rook defends it. After 1...Kf8, 2.Nxd5 wins the bishop.
ex.wp.own2: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.wp.own2.hint: The a1 rook is not playing yet. On which file does it find a target?
ex.wp.own2.solution: 1.Rd1! The a1 rook goes to the d-file and adds an attacker against the d5 bishop, already attacked by the knight. The bishop cannot move, because the rook would capture the d8 rook. After 1...f6, 2.Nxd5 wins the bishop.
ex.wp.own3: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.wp.own3.hint: Which black piece is not playing yet? On which file does it find a target?
ex.wp.own3.solution: 1...Rfd8! The f8 rook, stuck behind the f7 pawn, goes to the d-file and adds an attacker against the d4 bishop, which only the h4 rook defends. The bishop cannot move: it is pinned in front of the d1 king. After 2.Ke2, 2...Rxd4 wins the bishop.
ex.wp.9G9D5: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.wp.9G9D5.hint: The d1 rook does nothing on the d-file. Where is the black king?
ex.wp.9G9D5.solution: 19.Rdh1! The d1 rook doubles on the h-file and threatens mate on h8. After 19...g6, 20.Rh8+ Kg7 21.R1h7+ Kf6 22.Rxf8: White wins the rook.
ex.wp.OQDJk: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.wp.OQDJk.hint: The d6 rook attacks the d7 knight. Which white piece is not yet helping to attack it?
ex.wp.OQDJk.solution: 21.Rad1! The a1 rook doubles on the d-file against the d7 knight, which cannot move: after 21...Ne5, 22.Rd8+ Ke7 23.Rxh8. The black bishop blocks the file on d5, and 22.cxd5 captures it.
ex.wp.JVrTV: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.wp.JVrTV.hint: Count who attacks and who defends the d5 knight. Which of your pieces is not in that count yet?
ex.wp.JVrTV.solution: 23.Red1! The e1 rook goes to the d-file: three pieces attack the d5 knight, and only two defend it. After 23...Qc7, 24.Rxd5 wins the knight.
ex.wp.wLpR7: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.wp.wLpR7.hint: The h1 rook is not playing yet. Look at the e5 knight and what stands behind it.
ex.wp.wLpR7.solution: 18.Rhe1! The h1 rook doubles on the e-file against the e5 knight, which cannot move: behind it is the e8 rook. After 18...f6, which defends the knight, 19.f4 attacks it with the pawn, and it falls.
ex.kw.W2AT4: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.kw.W2AT4.hint: Look at the squares around the black king: which black piece defends g7?
ex.kw.W2AT4.solution: 17.Qxf6#! The queen captures the f6 bishop, the defender of g7, with mate: the h6 bishop guards g7, and the c4 bishop guards g8. If 17.Qxe8+, the a8 rook recaptures.
ex.kw.aP4L7: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.kw.aP4L7.hint: Look at the pawns that have advanced around the white king and at the b6 bishop.
ex.kw.aP4L7.solution: 16...Qxg3#! With the h-pawn on h3, g3 is no longer guarded by it; only the f2 pawn defends it, and that pawn is pinned by the b6 bishop. The queen captures the g3 pawn with mate, and the b7 bishop guards g2 and h1.
ex.kw.W08dE: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.kw.W08dE.hint: Black's g-pawn has left g7. Which squares did it leave unguarded?
ex.kw.W08dE.solution: 21.Qxh6#! The queen captures the h6 pawn with mate. Without the g7 pawn, nothing defends h6; the c4 bishop guards g8, and the queen guards g7 and h7.
ex.kw.KTbn9: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.kw.KTbn9.hint: The f6 pawn guards g7. Look for a way to open the h-file for the rook.
ex.kw.KTbn9.solution: 41.Qxh7+! The queen gives itself up on h7 and opens the h-file; the king has to capture, 41...Kxh7. 42.Rh4#: the f6 pawn guards g7, and g8 is occupied by the black rook. If 41.Rh4?, 41...Nf8 defends h7.
ex.kw.3FNce: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.kw.3FNce.hint: The e5 bishop guards h8 along the diagonal. Look for a way to open the h-file for the queen.
ex.kw.3FNce.solution: 21.Rxg6+! The rook captures the g6 pawn, which sheltered the king, and the h7 pawn recaptures, 21...hxg6 (if 21...Rg7, 22.Qxg7#). 22.Qh8#: the h-file has opened, and the e5 bishop defends the queen on h8 along the diagonal. If 21.exf5?, 21...Nxe5 captures the bishop; and after 21...hxg6, 22.Qxg6+? allows 22...Kf8.
ex.kw.0MWU8: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.kw.0MWU8.hint: The queen on h6 occupies a weak square, and the h3 rook supports the h-file.
ex.kw.0MWU8.solution: 17.Qxh7+! The queen captures the h7 pawn, defended by the h3 rook; the king only has 17...Kf8. 18.Qxf7#: the queen captures the f7 pawn, defended by the e5 knight.
ex.kw.0bDWl: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.kw.0bDWl.hint: The b3 bishop pins the f7 pawn, and the f6 pawn guards g7.
ex.kw.0bDWl.solution: 23.Qxg6+! The f7 pawn cannot recapture, pinned by the b3 bishop to the king; the king only has 23...Kh8. 24.Qg7#: the queen enters g7, the weak square defended by the f6 pawn. If 23.Qh6?, the c1 queen captures it.
ex.kw.NW0qQ: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.kw.NW0qQ.hint: The c3 queen aims along the diagonal all the way to h8. Look for a weak square near the king for the knight.
ex.kw.NW0qQ.solution: 28.Nh6+! The knight enters h6, the weak square the g-pawn left behind, with check; with the c3 queen on the diagonal to h8, the king only has 28...Kf8. 29.Qh8#: the queen comes in along the diagonal, and the h6 knight guards f7. If 28.Rxf3?, 28...Qg5 defends the king.
part.kingWeaknesses.title: Weaknesses around the king
part.kingWeaknesses.summary: A pawn that advances in front of the castled king leaves weak squares; the attacker trades off their defender and gets in, unless the opponent has defenders to spare.
